rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Chap XCII If one be Bewitched or not
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A new numbered chapter asks how to infer alleged bewitchment.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Supernatural harm is not established by this source.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: in a Question where suspicion of Witchcraft is
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The subject is an already suspected case, not an independent test for supernatural harm.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Prior suspicion risks confirmatory interpretation.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Twelfth ruler placed in sixth is given as one adverse configuration.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Astrological source claim only.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The reciprocal sixth ruler in twelfth is also listed.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Not a second observed patient.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The first ruler placed in twelfth is another alleged sign.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Planet position not independently recalculated.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The inverse twelfth lord in first is also treated adversely.
rules.original_source_qualifications: This is a directional alternative.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Eighth ruler in first is an additional alternative.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Different technical condition from twelfth placement.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The first ruler in eighth is another alternative testimony.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No measured diagnostic likelihood.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: it is probable otherwise not so
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly calls bewitchment probable in these configurations and otherwise not.
rules.original_source_qualifications: A two-sided historical decision rule, not evidence that bewitchment occurs.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He claims additional succeeding judgments are more certain than the first list.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Asserted certainty without independent calibration.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly invokes a purported learned rule from practitioners claiming esoteric expertise.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Authority appeal is not independent medical validation.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: one Planet Lord ascendant and twelfth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He describes a single planet governing both first and twelfth houses.
rules.original_source_qualifications: House-rulership relation, not a cause of illness.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Such a configuration is alleged to signal an illness beyond natural causes.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No clinical diagnosis or demonstration.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He specifically uses Saturn ruling both houses as an example.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Special Saturn subcase.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Retrograde Saturn in twelfth is one specified placement.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Planetary motion and placement not recalculated.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Alternatively Saturn retrograde in seventh or eighth is mentioned.
rules.original_source_qualifications: The exact scope of identical conditions is retained as a source caveat.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Moon, ruling sixth in this example, applies to Saturn.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Additional required relation.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Under this combination Lilly confidently labels the querent bewitched or under malefic speech.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical accusation, not independently verified occult action.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He alleges a spirit could cause oppression and distorted imagination.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Do not equate delirium, distress or illness with supernatural influence.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He specifically predicts disturbance of thought or imagination.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No independently documented mental status examination.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Combustion of the first ruler is treated as another warning.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Traditional astrology condition only.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: infortunate twelfth or joyned twelfth Lord
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Misfortune in twelfth or joining its lord is an alternate condition.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Additional possibilities weaken unique identification.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly conjectures the inquirer experiences severe fear or alleged enchantment.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source perception, not actual psychiatric diagnosis.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He suggests spirits may trouble the person.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Unverified supernatural claim.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A shared first/twelfth lord that is combust triggers another interpretive branch.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Different from simply combust ascendant lord.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He tells the astrologer to use the Sun's house rulership for attribution.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No independently validated perpetrator identification.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Signe quarter Heaven where he is
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He also uses sign and sky quadrant to suggest an alleged suspect's direction.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Geographical inference not tested.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He proposes locating the alleged witch in a derived direction.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Naming or locating someone based on this is not justified.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord ascendant Lord twelfth Combust or
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The sentence about combust shared first/twelfth lord continues across original PDF498–499.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Keep physical seam and source order without duplicate clauses.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Affliction by third-house lord is used as a further branch.
rules.original_source_qualifications: House third traditionally linked to neighbors/kin.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly suggests a neighbor or relative caused the supposed harm.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Unsupported accusation toward other people.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He derives presumed motives from the first ruler's house.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Not an observed motive.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He also examines the third ruler's placement to assign an alleged cause.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Different from first-ruler placement.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He attributes possible disputes to pasture or small livestock under sixth-house conditions.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Period agricultural examples, not a verified conflict.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A quarrel over a hired servant is another proposed cause.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Alternative motive rather than proven perpetration.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly advises interpreting other house contexts as needed.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Very flexible causal classification; no unique observable endpoint.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Affliction of the first ruler by sixth lord is given another alleged source.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Technical relation distinct from third-house accusation.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He names a woman who sells ale, a nurse, or a drunken acquaintance as possible instigator.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historically stigmatizing conjecture; no identified person.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord tenth afflict Lord ascendant twelfth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Affliction of the first ruler in twelfth by tenth lord is considered.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Additional distinct chart condition.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He offers divine or supernatural causation under the tenth-house branch.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Religious attribution not a demonstrated mechanism.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord ascendant Mars or Saturn twelfth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A first ruler that is Mars/Saturn in twelfth is described as adverse.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical malefic planets; no medical diagnostic validity.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Combustion and negative contact with twelfth lord are added.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Further conditions, not observable witchcraft evidence.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The combination is said to indicate an ordinary witch.
rules.original_source_qualifications: False accusation risk; no authenticated perpetrator.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Twelfth lord's presence in first is restated.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Another interpretation of a condition also in opening list.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He allows either evil spirits or people's malicious speech as an explanation.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Alternative agents include ordinary gossip, not established supernatural harm.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly generalizes from communities he characterizes as troubled by witches.
rules.original_source_qualifications: An author's belief about prevalence, not verified incidence.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He uses Moon in twelfth opposed to first ruler or twelfth ruler as additional testimony.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source claims do not support identifying a person.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: For large cattle he reassigns the subject's derived ascendant to the original twelfth.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Derived-house change, not a new real patient.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He then treats the original eleventh as the cattle's twelfth.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Dependent on previous derived-house assignment.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly instructs adjusting the rules to circumstances.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Interpretive latitude reduces falsifiability.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: An unnumbered section headed natural remedies follows the accusations within the same printed chapter.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Not evidence that a magical diagnosis or treatment works.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly presupposes that a horary figure can describe a supposed instigator.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Unproven identity; must not be used to accuse anyone.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord twelfth or posited twelfth malignant aspect
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He invokes twelfth-house ruler/occupant afflicting the first ruler as a prerequisite.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Technical relation, not causality.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He recommends timing a household counter-ritual around the whereabouts of a suspected person.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Potential risk of harassment or scapegoating; not modern guidance.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The remedy instructions start at the foot of PDF499 and continue on PDF500.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Preserve single ritual across the physical page seam.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He describes using material from a doorway and a heated household surface.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical ritual only; do not replicate dangerous heating or fire exposure.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The proposed human ritual involves bodily liquid and a very hot tile.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Burn and contamination hazards; no treatment evidence.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: let no body come into house
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The author includes isolation/timing conditions during the supposed ritual.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Not a medically relevant efficacy control.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Cattle bewitched ... Haire of every one
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He describes animal-hair materials in a ritual aimed at alleged livestock bewitchment.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No veterinary diagnosis or benefit substantiated.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He reports exposing those materials to fire or heated tiles.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Fire, smoke, and animal handling risks.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The ritual ends by associating ashes and burial direction with an alleged suspect's location.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Not an actual validated method for identifying or treating a cattle illness.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He offers a variation involving thatch instead of roof tile.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Alternative historical material, not independent successful patient.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He also describes a salt-containing variation using fire.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No substantiated benefit and may be hazardous.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: An alternative household ritual uses heated metal objects.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Physical burn and fire hazards; not a medical intervention.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He describes a ritual involving heating a bodily-fluid sample.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Burn/contamination hazards; no validated therapy.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The variant includes nails and salt with the other materials.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Documented object identities only, not stepwise instructions for use.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly suggests lunar phases influence the ritual's effectiveness.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No controlled evidence for timing effect.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The author gives another livestock-hair variation.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No veterinary efficacy demonstrated.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly claims he has found the sympathetic experiments work.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Uncorroborated practitioner assertion without authenticated cases.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He characterizes the proposed approach as working through sympathy.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical theoretical explanation, not demonstrated mechanism.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He says many more procedures could be given and appeals to experience.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Not a systematic study of outcomes or harm.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly closes the subsection with a Latin maxim whose exact wording and argumentative role require separate philological checking.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No confident literal translation or inference of empirical method is admitted from this scan alone.
